/-!
# Convergence of the Borwein Series with Sinusoidal Coefficient

*References:*
- [MathWorld, Harmonic Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/HarmonicSeries.html)
- Borwein, J.; Bailey, D.; Girgensohn, R. *Experimentation in Mathematics: Computational Paths
  to Discovery*, A K Peters, 2004, p. 56.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BorweinSineSeries

/--
Does the series
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}\sin n\right)^n}{n}
$$
converge?

After computing approximately $10^7$ terms, the partial sums approximate $2.163$.

See https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11017 for a proof of the convergence,
relying on an irrationality measure for pi.

Also see
https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/docs/BorweinSineSeries.md
for a partial formalization of the conjecture,
conditional on such an irrationality measure of pi (cf https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.06345).
-/
@[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean",  AMS 26 40]
theorem borwein_sine_series :
    answer(True) ↔
      Summable fun n : ℕ+ ↦ ((2 / 3 + 1 / 3 * Real.sin (n : ℝ)) ^ (n : ℕ)) / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end BorweinSineSeries

status_issues.recorded: An unconditional formal_proof using lean4 annotation points to AxiomMath's BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean.
status_issues.source_status: The cited Lean proof is conditional: its final theorem requires hpi : PiIrrBound. That bound is defined but not proved in the linked file. The unconditional convergence claim is nevertheless established informally by Boppana, so research solved and answer(True) are correct.
status_issues.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean, lines 801–804: `theorem borwein_sine_series (hpi : PiIrrBound) : Summable ...`. Lines 5–10 define PiIrrBound as the existence of C > 0 and Q₀ such that C / q^7.10321 < |π - p/q| for all integer p and positive natural q ≥ Q₀. The source proves the implication from this bound, not the bound itself.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep the mathematical statement, research solved category, and answer(True). Record the external proof with `conditional formal_proof ... assuming ...`, naming a separate declaration of the required pi bound, or remove the unconditional formal-proof annotation until a complete proof is linked.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses unconditional Summable over ℕ+, whereas the source asks whether the ordered series from n = 1 to infinity converges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every positive integer n, -1 ≤ sin n ≤ 1 gives 1/3 ≤ 2/3 + (1/3) sin n ≤ 1, so the summand is positive. For nonnegative real terms, convergence of ordered partial sums is equivalent to unconditional summability. Reindexing ℕ+ by k ↦ k+1 gives precisely the source's terms. The full equivalence, including the explicit summand and True ↔ wrapper, was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted Borwein theorem; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
